caution: These anchors are NOT equivalent to the food risks on this site. Each one is measured on its own basis - some are per year, some are over a whole lifetime, some are per single event - while the food figures are per serving eaten. They are here to give a feel for how big or small a number like '1 in 100,000' actually is, not to say that eating a salad is 'the same as' any of them. Comparing across different bases is the single easiest way to mislead yourself with risk numbers.

anchors.note: CDC estimates roughly 1 in 6 Americans - about 48 million people - get a foodborne illness each year, from all causes combined.
